**Observation notes:**

- **Plant part affected:** Banana leaf (visible parallel venation, broad blade)
- **Lesion features:**
  - Single, isolated, relatively large lesion
  - Very dark brown/black necrotic center (almost opaque black core)
  - Surrounded by a distinct reddish-orange/rusty-brown halo/ring
  - Irregular but somewhat angular/arrowhead shape
  - Well-defined border between lesion and surrounding green leaf tissue
  - Some yellowing visible at the bottom leaf margin

**Ruling out other classes:**
- **Bunchy_Top:** Viral disease; causes stunted growth, narrow leaves, dark green streaking — no match.
- **Cigar_End_Rot:** Affects banana fruit tips (finger ends), not leaves — no match.
- **Panama_Disease:** Fusarium wilt causing systemic yellowing/wilting — not a localized leaf spot.
- **Anthracnose:** Usually sunken, dark spots more common on fruit/stems; halo pattern less pronounced.
- **Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka:** Lesions typically begin as pale yellow streaks, mature into gray-centered spots with yellow halos — the center here is jet black, not gray, and the halo is reddish-orange, not yellow.

**Best match — Cordana Leaf Spot (Cordana musae):**
The hallmark of Cordana leaf spot is an oval-to-irregular dark brown/black necrotic center surrounded by a characteristic reddish-brown to orange ring/halo on banana leaves. This precisely matches the lesion seen — the deep black core with the vivid reddish-orange concentric border is the textbook presentation of this fungal disease.
